rows.role_title: Vice-President of the Federative Republic of Brazil
rows.text: The publication's introduction says that since 1891 the Vice-Presidency has been held by 26 Vice-Presidents and that its succession chronology shows the office left vacant ('o cargo ficou vago') on ten occasions, by ascent to the Presidency following a vacancy or by a break in institutional order. Its 'Cronologia sucessória' graphic places José Sarney at 1985 followed by a grey segment before Itamar Franco at 1990, and a grey segment between 1992 and 1995 before the next Vice-President; a footnote says the graphic is a visual reference not proportional to time.

locator.item: 'CRONOLOGIA SUCESSÓRIA - Vice-Presidência da República'; introduction box; footnote (1) on pdf p. 7

rows.role_title: Vice-President of the Federative Republic of Brazil
rows.text: The profile of José Sarney gives his period as Vice-President as 15/03/1985 to 21/04/1985, with Tancredo de Almeida Neves as President, and says that Tancredo died before taking office and Sarney assumed the office on 21 April 1985.

rows.role_title: Vice-President of the Federative Republic of Brazil
rows.text: The profile of Itamar Franco gives his period as Vice-President as 15/03/1990 to 29/12/1992, with Fernando Afonso Collor de Melo as President, and says that on Collor's removal by the impeachment process he assumed the office of President provisionally ('em caráter provisório') on 2 October 1992 and was confirmed ('efetivado') in it on 29 December 1992 after Collor's resignation.

rows.role_title: Vice-President of the Federative Republic of Brazil
rows.text: The Vice-Presidency's profile of Michel Temer gives his period as Vice-President as 01/01/2011 to 31/08/2016, with Dilma Vana Rousseff as President; it says he was elected Vice-President in 2010 and re-elected in 2014, and that he assumed the Presidency 'definitivamente' on 31 August 2016 after the Senate approved the impeachment process and removed Rousseff.

rows.role_title: Vice-President of the Federative Republic of Brazil
rows.text: In the Vice-Presidency's 'Cronologia sucessória' graphic, Michel Temer is placed at 2011 and a grey, unlabelled segment beginning at 2016 precedes Hamilton Mourão at 2019; footnote (1) says the illustration is a visual reference not proportional in time.

locator.section: 'CRONOLOGIA SUCESSÓRIA - Vice-Presidência da República', bottom rows (2011, 2016, 2019, 2023) on pdf p. 6; footnote (1) on pdf p. 7

rows.role_title: Vice-President of the Federative Republic of Brazil
rows.text: The profile of Hamilton Mourão gives his period as Vice-President as 01/01/2019 to 31/12/2022, with Jair Messias Bolsonaro as President, and says the ticket was elected in the second round on 28 October 2018 and that on 1 January 2019 he became Vice-President of the Republic.

rows.role_title: Vice-President of the Federative Republic of Brazil
rows.text: The profile of Geraldo José Rodrigues Alckmin Filho says that since 1 January 2023 he is the 26th Vice-President of the Federative Republic of Brazil, elected in 2022 for the period 2023-2026 with President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva; its header box gives 01/01/2023 to 31/12/2026, and the colophon lists him as Vice-President.

locator.section: header box '01/01/2023 a 31/12/2026'; paragraphs 1 and 5; colophon on pdf p. 2
